item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a clean, independent 2024 example in the indexed material of Modi lying under oath to Parliament or a court. Most negative evidence comes from campaign/public messaging, state information control, and pressure on media, not from documented false testimony in a formal legal setting. So the strongest defensible claim is not “proved habitual liar in every arena,” but rather “repeatedly willing to use misleading communal messaging and information control when it served power, while remaining procedurally compliant in some formal diplomatic and electoral settings.”","evidence":[{"title":"Accepted coalition rule after electoral setback","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"4 Jun 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-set-to-win-historic-third-term-but-with-surprisingly-slim-majority/2116973/","summary":"Reuters reported that the BJP fell short of a solo majority and Modi framed the result as a coalition mandate. This is relevant because it is a self-defense statement against an allegation that would damage reputation; the denial is counterevidence only if one accepts the surrounding reporting as more credible.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.8","6B.10"]},{"title":"Campaign rhetoric linked Muslims to a false redistribution narrative","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"22 Apr 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-congress-seeks-action-against-modi-for-comments-about-muslims/2051980/","summary":"Reuters reported that Modi said Congress wanted to redistribute Hindu wealth to Muslims and referred to Muslims as “infiltrators.” That is strong evidence of misleading or deceptive political messaging designed to protect power by inflaming fear.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.8","6B.10"]},{"title":"Shifted from development talk to communal attack messaging","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"23 Apr 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/india/indias-modi-calls-rivals-pro-muslim-as-election-campaign-changes-tack/2053223/","summary":"Reuters described Modi pivoting away from development messaging toward anti-Muslim attacks and wealth-redistribution warnings. This supports a finding of willingness to use deceptive or inflammatory messaging rather than straightforward truth-telling.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.8"]},{"title":"Fact-check unit attempted state information control","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"21 Mar 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/india/india-top-court-puts-on-hold-unit-for-fact-checking-online-content-about-govt/2009612/","summary":"The government created a fact-checking unit with power to flag content about government business as false or misleading; the Supreme Court stayed it. This does not prove Modi lied, but it is strong evidence that the administration was willing to control truth claims about itself when that protected power.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.9","6B.8"]},{"title":"Pressure on the independent press and foreign correspondents","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"13 Nov 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/news/inside-modis-crackdown-foreign-press-india","summary":"The Reuters Institute reported visa and work-permit denials and pressure on foreign correspondents critical of the government. That is indirect but meaningful evidence against a truth-telling habit, because governments that are comfortable with the truth rarely need to intimidate the messengers.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.9","6B.8"]},{"title":"Press freedom concerns and regulatory pressure","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"17 Jun 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/india","summary":"Reuters Institute noted new laws, broad regulatory powers, and the NewsClick raids as chilling press freedom. This is not direct lying, but it is evidence of transactional politics that often accompanies selective truth-telling and public spin.","question_ids":["7B.1","6B.9","6B.10"]}]}
